intro: Written in spring 1965 from a much longer draft, cut down to six minutes, and released as a single many thought far too long for radio. It reached number two in the US. Six decades on it is still in the set, with more than 2000 performances on record.

lives.title: Waltz time
lives.note: The first attempts were in three-four time, led by piano. A waltz-time rehearsal later surfaced on The Bootleg Series Vol. 1–3, and the full sessions on The Cutting Edge.

lives.title: The master take
lives.note: Back in four-four the next day, with Al Kooper improvising the organ part that became the song's signature. Released as a single in July 1965, then as the opening track of Highway 61 Revisited.

lives.title: First time on stage
lives.note: Played loud with members of the Paul Butterfield Blues Band, in the short electric set that drew boos from parts of the crowd. This is the first performance of the song on record.

lives.title: Manchester, after the heckle
lives.note: Someone in the audience shouts "Judas!". He answers, turns to the Hawks, and they play the song as loud as they can. Released in 1998 as The Bootleg Series Vol. 4, long mislabelled as the Royal Albert Hall concert.

lives.title: Isle of Wight
lives.note: His first full concert in three years, with the Band, in a gentler, country-tinged arrangement. It ended up on Self Portrait.

lives.title: Stadium-sized
lives.note: Back on the road after eight years, shouted and driven hard. Released on Before the Flood. The 1974 shows are not in this site's concert data yet.

lives.title: Unplugged
lives.note: Recorded for MTV with a small acoustic band, slower and warmer, and released on MTV Unplugged.

others.note: Played it at the Monterey Pop Festival in June 1967.
Recorded it for their 1995 live album Stripped.
